title: Writing and running free-threaded race tests (tests/test_freethreaded.py)
answers: how to test pydantic thread safety on no-GIL Python
reproduce a race condition in pydantic tests
body:
Race tests go in tests/test_freethreaded.py. The module-level `pytestmark` skips them unless `tests/conftest.py:is_free_threaded` is true (`not sys._is_gil_enabled()`, which is False on older Pythons) and also skips on emscripten. On a normal GIL build they are reported as skipped. To actually run them, use a free-threaded interpreter such as python3.14t.
Use the `run_concurrently(setup, target, rounds=100, threads=8)` helper. `setup()` builds a fresh class for each round, and `target(ctx, index)` runs in all threads at once, released together by a threading.Barrier. Use `index` to give one thread a different role, for example index 0 rebuilds while the others instantiate.
Tricks for making a race show up reliably: add thousands of attributes to the class (setattr in a loop) so iterating it takes longer. Leave a forward ref undefined at class creation so no annotations cache gets set, then define it with `monkeypatch.setitem(globals(), ...)` so that ForwardRef.evaluate reads the namespace.
applies: Tests for concurrency/thread-safety of pydantic schema building
